title: Support Inbox
intro: Ten messages from "support" teams, one minute. Your crypto apps have been busy.
Swipe left if it is a scam, right if it is safe. Or tap the buttons.
Careful: some are honest. Do not cry wolf.

cards.text: Your Zelvora login code is 482917. Never share it with anyone, including Zelvora staff.
cards.why: You asked for a code, it tells you not to share it, and it asks for nothing else.

cards.text: Your withdrawals are paused. Sign in here and enter your 2-step code within 1 hour: zelvora-unlock.co/login
cards.why: A login link, a deadline and a request for your 2-step code. Real alerts live in the app.

cards.text: We saw your post. Send us your 12-word phrase and we will fix your wallet right now.
cards.why: No real support ever asks for your recovery phrase. It is the key to all your coins.

cards.text: Hedrio 3.1 is out. Update from your phone's official app store. Nothing else to do.
cards.why: It points to the official app store and asks for nothing.

cards.text: Withdrawal of 0.4 BTC to a new address requested. Not you? Call +44 20 7946 0000 now.
cards.why: A frightening withdrawal and a phone number in the text. Check the number inside your own app.

cards.text: Welcome to the club! Rules are pinned. Admins never DM first or ask for money or phrases.
cards.why: It gives rules and asks for nothing. It even warns you about scams.

cards.text: We can recover your lost coins. Pay a 10% fee first. Guaranteed.
cards.why: A recovery promise with a fee up front is a second scam on top of the first.

cards.text: You enabled a new withdrawal address. If this was not you, open the app and lock your account.
cards.why: It tells you something you did, and sends you to your own app.

cards.text: LIVE: send 0.1 BTC to the QR code and get 0.2 BTC back. 20 minutes left!
cards.why: Send-and-double is the oldest crypto scam. Nobody gives coins back for free.

cards.text: Your monthly statement is ready in the app. No action needed.
cards.why: It asks for nothing and points to the app you already use.

golden_rule: Real support never asks for your recovery phrase or 2-step code. Check inside your own app.

quick_check.q: A message from "support" says your withdrawals are paused and you must enter your 2-step code on a link. What do you do?

options.text: Enter the code, it is only a check
Do not click. Open the app yourself and report the message
Reply and ask for a phone number
Forward it to friends as a warning, with the link

quick_check.explain: The link and the request for your code are the signs. Your own app is the only safe place to check.
